fr:title.text: Curried Vertical Exponentials via a Section-Parameterised Endofunctor

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Curried Vertical Exponentials via a Section-Parameterised Endofunctor

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Notes on whether the curried displayed-presheaf vertical exponential _⇒PshSmallⱽ_ can be defined and given a UMP without detouring through the uncurried machinery in Displayed/Presheaf/Uncurried/.

fr:title.text: The uncurried definition reveals the right primitive

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: The uncurried definition reveals the right primitive

fr:mainmatter.html:p: In Uncurried/Constructions/Exponential.agda, the small vertical exponential is
fr:mainmatter.html:pre: _⇒ⱽPshSmall_ : Presheafᴰ P Cᴰ ℓQᴰ _⇒ⱽPshSmall_ = reindPsh ×LRⱽPshᴰ Qᴰ
fr:mainmatter.html:p: where \times \mathrm {LR}^\vee \mathrm {Psh}^\dagger : (\mathcal {C}^\dagger / P) \to (\mathcal {C}^\dagger / P) is the "thicken with P^\dagger " endofunctor on the displayed category of elements, sending (\Gamma , \Gamma ^\dagger , p) \mapsto (\Gamma , \Gamma ^\dagger \times ^\vee p^* P^\dagger , p). The exponential is then just precomposition of Q^\dagger with this endofunctor.

In the curried setting (Constructions/Exponential/Base.agda) the object/hom data are already defined and pointwise agree with the uncurried version, but the β/η in UniversalProperty.agda:184--219 are stuck. The reason is that the curried definition is built directly as a Functorᴰ, so every β/η step has to redo the functoriality bookkeeping that the precompose-with-an-endofunctor abstraction would discharge once.
The curried analog factors through a new abstraction. Roughly:
fr:mainmatter.html:pre: record EndoFunctorⱽ (P : Presheaf C ℓP) (Cᴰ : Categoryᴰ C ℓCᴰ ℓCᴰ') : Type _ where field F-obⱽ : ∀ {Γ} → P.p[ Γ ] → Cᴰ.ob[ Γ ] → Cᴰ.ob[ Γ ] F-homⱽ : ∀ {Γ Δ γ p} {Γᴰ Δᴰ} → (γᴰ : Cᴰ [ γ ][ Δᴰ , Γᴰ ]) → Cᴰ [ γ ][ F-obⱽ (γ P.⋆ p) Δᴰ , F-obⱽ p Γᴰ ] -- + identity / composition coherence
fr:mainmatter.html:p: Reindexing along such an F is
fr:mainmatter.html:pre: (F *ᴰ Qᴰ).F-obᴰ Γᴰ p = Qᴰ.F-obᴰ (F-obⱽ p Γᴰ) p
fr:mainmatter.html:p: which is the curried analog of reindPsh. From a LocallyRepresentableⱽ Pᴰ you get a canonical \times P^\dagger : \mathrm {EndoFunctor}^\vee P\, \mathcal {C}^\dagger sending (\Gamma ^\dagger , p) \mapsto \Gamma ^\dagger \times ^\vee p^* P^\dagger , and the curried exponential becomes P^\dagger \Rightarrow Q^\dagger := \times P^\dagger \mathbin {*}^\dagger Q^\dagger , definitionally equal to the existing definition. β/η then factor as a generic naturality lemma about \mathbin {*}^\dagger (purely formal) plus the universal property of \times P^\dagger , which the existing LocallyRepresentableⱽNotation calculus already supplies.

fr:title.text: Why a plain Functorᴰ over Id\_C does not suffice

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Why a plain Functorᴰ over Id\_C does not suffice

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Tempting alternative: just use a Functorᴰ Cᴰ Cᴰ over \mathrm {Id}_{\mathcal {C}}. This fails because the thickening genuinely depends on the section p.

\times P^\dagger sends (\Gamma ^\dagger , p) \mapsto \Gamma ^\dagger \times ^\vee p^* P^\dagger : the displayed object you produce depends on which section you are thickening with respect to. A Functorᴰ Cᴰ Cᴰ over \mathrm {Id}_{\mathcal {C}} has no access to p, only to \Gamma ^\dagger . Reindexing Q^\dagger along it would yield (\Gamma ^\dagger , p) \mapsto Q^\dagger (F\, \Gamma ^\dagger , p), where the thickening is independent of the section — wrong shape.

The uncurried side gets away with a plain \mathrm {Functor}\, (\mathcal {C}^\dagger / P)\, (\mathcal {C}^\dagger / P) because the section is baked into the base. The curried analog must expose p as an explicit parameter, which is exactly what the proposed EndoFunctorⱽ does. The pure-displayed-functor formulation that is equivalent — Functorᴰ (reind π* Cᴰ) (reind π* Cᴰ) over \mathrm {Id}_{\int P} — is just the uncurried side under a different name.

If \mathcal {C}^\dagger is a fibration, vertical exponentials reduce to the classical formulation: each fiber is cartesian closed, and reindexing functors f^* are CC functors (preserve products and exponentials, i.e. Beck--Chevalley). Skip the displayed-presheaf machinery entirely.
Precedent already exists in Uncurried/Constructions/Exponential.agda:394:
fr:mainmatter.html:pre: BinProductsⱽ+Fibration→AllLRⱽ : BinProductsⱽ Cᴰ → isFibration Cᴰ → AllLRⱽ
fr:mainmatter.html:p: The exponential analog should be: fiber-CC + f^* preserves exponentials → Exponentialsⱽ. β/η in each fiber are ordinary CCC β/η, and BC gives naturality across fibers.

Trade-off: most use cases in this library (logical relations, glueing, syntactic models) have fibered \mathcal {C}^\dagger , so this should be the primary definition with the locally-representable formulation derived as the general case. The locally-representable version remains necessary for non-fibered \mathcal {C}^\dagger , e.g. categories of elements (\mathcal {C}^\dagger / P) for arbitrary P, which are not generally fibered.

The β/η that stall in the curried setting stall on reind bookkeeping that comes from \mathrm {id} \cdot f \neq f judgmentally. Yoneda strictification makes this judgmental and thus unsticks the proofs directly, without introducing new abstractions. See Yoneda Strictification: Tradeoffs and Opportunities for the tradeoffs of that approach. The two routes are not mutually exclusive: one could introduce EndoFunctorⱽ as the right abstraction and use strictification internally to discharge its naturality lemmas.

fr:title.text: Displayed strictness, reindexing, and gluing via UMP

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Displayed strictness, reindexing, and gluing via UMP

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Companion to the Yoneda strictification tradeoffs note and the strictification parent, recording three observations from extending YonedaStrictifyᴰ with round-trip natural isos and thinking about how to actually use it for gluing.

Displayed strictness is not implied by base strictness. Even with \cdot \mathrm {Assoc} = \mathrm {refl} on \mathcal {C}, the displayed associator \cdot \mathrm {Assoc}^\dagger is a separate definitional equality between displayed composites (f^\dagger \cdot g^\dagger ) \cdot h^\dagger and f^\dagger \cdot (g^\dagger \cdot h^\dagger ). Strict base only collapses the ≡[ ] index to a homogeneous ≡ — it does not make the displayed terms reduce. YonedaStrictifyᴰ Cᴰ delivers strict displayed laws by composing displayed presheaf homomorphisms as functions, the same trick as the base.

Reindexing transports strict laws only along strict functors. Reindexing C^\dagger along F : D \to C produces a displayed category whose composition law involves both C^\dagger .\cdot \mathrm {Assoc}^\dagger and the witnesses F.\mathrm {F\text {-}seq}, F.\mathrm {F\text {-}id}. For the reindexed law to hold by refl, both sides must be refl. A functor between strict categories need not be strict in this sense — F-id and F-seq are independent of the codomain's laws and depend on how the functor is defined. The relevant special case is the recursor F : \mathrm {Syn} \to \mathrm {YonedaStrictify}\,\mathcal {C} for a syntactic QIIT: it maps the syntactic identity/composition constructors directly to \mathrm {id}/\cdot in the target, so F-id/F-seq reduce to refl, and the equation-constructor cases of the recursor go through precisely because the target's laws are themselves refl.

Gluing-via-UMP pipeline. The shape we actually want for a gluing proof is: (i) build the relevant vertical structure (CCC, dependent products, etc.) on YonedaStrictifyᴰ Cᴰ, where the displayed laws are refl; (ii) get a strict recursor F : \mathrm {Syn} \to \mathrm {YonedaStrictify}\,\mathcal {C} from the universal property of syntax; (iii) reindex the displayed structure along F — strict because of (1) + (2), so the UMP survives reindexing; (iv) apply the global elimination principle on the reindexed displayed category to get a section; (v) transfer back through the round-trip natural iso from-to-YonedaStrictify. The delicate step is not reindexing back to the non-strict \mathcal {C} mid-proof — do that only at the boundary, after the section is in hand.

This sharpens the strategy sketched in sss-00BL and sss-00BM: strictification's payoff for gluing comes specifically from making the recursor strict, which lets reindexing carry the vertical universal properties intact.

We can define a Yoneda strictification operation and take displayed categories over that, or similarly we can use the extra identity category that Max created. None of this strictification can get rid of the transport in the (uncurried) displayed representable.

See Yoneda Strictification: Tradeoffs and Opportunities for tradeoffs and opportunities of the Yoneda strictification approach (with comparison to Type Theory in Type Theory using a Strictified Syntax), and Curried Vertical Exponentials via a Section-Parameterised Endofunctor for a related discussion of curried vertical exponentials and where strictification fits relative to introducing new abstractions.

Companion to Strictification. Notes from a session sketching what the YonedaStrictify construction in Categories/Instances/Strictify.agda buys us, what it costs, and what new constructions it makes plausible.

YonedaStrictify C has the same objects as \mathcal {C} but takes hom-sets to be strict natural transformations between representables \mathcal {C}[-, c]. Identity is the identity transformation and composition is function composition, so \cdot \cdot \mathrm {id}, \mathrm {id} \cdot \cdot , and associativity hold judgmentally (refl). toYonedaStrictify and fromYonedaStrictify give an equivalence to the original \mathcal {C}, but not an isomorphism: the round-trip uses \mathcal {C}.\mathrm {id} and \cdot \mathrm {IdR}.

The companion FiberOverStrictify.agda observes that for Categoryᴰ (YonedaStrictify C), the displayed and vertical compositions collapse: _⋆ᴰⱽ_ and _⋆ⱽᴰ_ need no reind, and identity laws hold by ∫Cᴰ.⋆IdL / ⋆IdR composed with rectifyOut rather than long reind-filler chains.
The naive view is "we have an equivalence, transport everything back, no loss." That's only true for equivalence-invariant content.

html:ul.html:li: Universe levels jump. Hom-sets in YonedaStrictify C live at \ell _C \sqcup \ell _{C'} rather than \ell _{C'}. Anything proved on the strict side carries that level back. For locally-small \mathcal {C} this can contaminate downstream universe-sensitive constructions.

Judgmental computation only on the strict side. If the motivation for strictifying was on-the-nose computation, transporting the result to the original \mathcal {C} turns refl back into a propositional path through the equivalence. The strictness lives where you build, not where you consume.

Strict preservation properties don't transport. "Functor F strictly preserves products" weakens to "preserves up to natural iso" after crossing the equivalence. For applications that need on-the-nose preservation (syntactic models, CwFs with strict substitution), this defeats the purpose.

Concrete handles on data. A morphism f : \mathcal {C}_0[A,B] lifts to \lambda c\, z \mapsto z \cdot f, a natural family. Pattern-matching or computation against the underlying f is gone; you reason via universal properties.

API costs at the boundary. Every consumer expecting a result about \mathcal {C}_0 either also strictifies or pays a transport. The cost propagates outward: bifunctors, profunctors, fibrations, limits all need to/fromYonedaStrictify insertions.
Specific limit/colimit objects are only iso to the strict-side limit, not equal to it. For formalization that wants "the syntactic context Γ is this list," this matters.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: So: existential and equivalence-invariant content survives intact; strict, concrete, or universe-sensitive content does not.

html:ul.html:li: Clean β/η for vertical exponentials. The proofs in Constructions/Exponential/UniversalProperty.agda that stall on reind-filler bookkeeping (see Slow Chains of Fillers for Reindexings for Instantiating Vertical Exponentials, An Idea at Fixing Concrete Performance Issues) should go through with the strict base, since the offending equations are identity-composition laws.
Collapse of displayed/vertical composition. _⋆ᴰⱽ_ and _⋆ⱽᴰ_ become a single operation; mixed associativity laws become refl. Every proof crossing the displayed/vertical boundary simplifies.
Beck--Chevalley as refl. For fibrations with strict reindexing, BC squares for substitution-stable structure could hold judgmentally, yielding something closer to a strict 2-category of fibrations.

Curry/Uncurry as a definitional bijection. The CurryPshᴰIso between curried and uncurried displayed presheaves involves reind-filler rectifications; over a strict base it should become a bijection that's refl on the round-trip.

Strict CwF / model-of-type-theory layer. Bridge to Kaposi--Pujet: a CwF over YonedaStrictify C would have substitution composing refl-strictly. This is the same move their QIIT-syntax line uses, just internally to one category rather than as a global strict syntax. See Type Theory in Type Theory using a Strictified Syntax.

Strict 2-category structure on Cat itself. Yoneda-strictifying every category gives a strictly associative 2-category of functors and NatTrans, useful for double-categorical / multicategorical work where coherence is the bottleneck.
Cleaner profunctor calculus. Coend-based composition has propositional unitor/associator. Over strict bases, parts of this become refl.
Glueing. Glueing constructions in Gluing/ use "rectify substitution" steps. Worth checking whether the existing infrastructure simplifies over a strict base.

Staged strategy: strictify internally, expose externally. Use YonedaStrictify only inside the proofs of difficult universal properties; export the resulting structure transported back to \mathcal {C}_0. The public API stays in \mathcal {C}_0, the hard proofs get the win, the boundary cost is paid in one place.

fr:mainmatter.html:p: See Type Theory in Type Theory using a Strictified Syntax. The technical move is the same: replace a structure with propositional equations by an equivalent one with judgmental ones, via Yoneda-style embedding into a functor category where laws hold by function-composition unitality and associativity.

The asymmetry is scope. They strictify the entire substitution calculus of dependent type theory, and the strict version is the canonical object — there is no "translate back to a non-strict syntax" because the strict syntax IS the syntax. Coherence cost is paid once, internally.

We strictify a single category internally to a richer (cubical) metatheory. The original \mathcal {C}_0 still exists, downstream code expects it, and every boundary between strict-side proofs and non-strict consumers requires mediation. The coherence cost is paid at the boundary, repeatedly.

This suggests a scaling principle: strictification pays off proportionally to how much of the surrounding library can be expressed natively over the strict base. If \mathcal {C}_0 is one of many displayed categories composed through the same metatheory, the boundary cost dominates. If the bulk of formalization can live natively over YonedaStrictify C, the move becomes worthwhile — at which point the question shifts to whether the strict version should be promoted to canonical, à la Kaposi--Pujet.

fr:title.text: Open question: does it eliminate the displayed-representable transport?

fr:frontmatter.fr:title: Open question: does it eliminate the displayed-representable transport?

fr:mainmatter.html:p: Strictification notes that strictification "cannot get rid of the transport in the (uncurried) displayed representable." This is a real obstruction: the elements category (\mathcal {C}^\dagger / P) carries a triangle equation \gamma \cdot p \equiv q as part of its morphism data, and that equation remains propositional even after the base is strictified. Strictifying the base flattens identity/associativity reinds but leaves the section-relation reinds untouched.
Worth tracking whether a parallel strictification on the section side (or a different definition of (\mathcal {C}^\dagger / P) using a homotopy-quotient-style equality) eliminates that one too.
